T4.2.message: viśva is marked as an adjective with the sense 'all, every, whole, entire, universal', but its meaning is the noun 'universe', and c2 reads it as viśvasya nāthaḥ 'Lord of the universe'. The pos and sense don't match the meaning. 'Lord of all' would also be a valid reading, so a human should choose: either the noun sense 'n. the whole world, universe' (mw-vishva.md) with pos noun, or keep the adjective and change the meaning to 'all'.

The sense recorded is MW's first sense, 'a mark, spot, sign, token...', but the meaning just says 'liṅga' without saying which sense is meant. Here the word describes jagat, a world that arises from Śiva, stays in Him and dissolves in Him. mw-linga.md has senses that may fit better: the Śiva-liṅga sense, and (Kap.) 'anything having an origin and therefore liable to be destroyed again'. gitapress-stotraratnavali.md translates it 'लिंगस्वरूप समस्त जगत्' and also leaves it unexplained. A human should decide which sense is meant and record that sense.
